releases.name: v0.16.14 — Git identity commits and validation binding recovery
releases.body:
# v0.16.14 — Git identity commits and validation binding recovery

## Changes

- Recognize commits with invocation-local `-c user.name=<literal>` and `-c user.email=<literal>` settings. Keep native Location/workdir whole-index inspection, preceding explicit adds, caller prohibitions and parallel Git-mutation restrictions. Arbitrary Git configuration, repository/index overrides, unsupported commit forms and active substitutions remain refused.
- Preserve Git ambiguity for Bash input/output process substitutions, including internal separators. Quoted literal values and non-Git native investigative commands retain their existing behavior.
- Explain exit-zero validation failures when declared read inputs change during execution. Direct completion retains the specific recovery instruction: inspect real inputs/outputs, prepare genuine generated inputs, or repair an estimated output-only read scope in the same Mission. Historical failed checks and freshness requirements are not relaxed.
- Correct cwd-only validation registration when the initial frozen contract already contains an explicit cwd. Keep frozen JSON property order across external/original/omitted/restored cwd registrations without changing admission identity, budget, source scope or old evidence.

## Review and verification

- PR #346: root source inspection and existing completed GitHub code/security reviews found no outstanding findings. Its earlier development SourceReview found process-substitution paths; the final head includes their corrections and regressions. The correcting reviewer's self-recheck is not a separate independent post-fix approval.
- PR #347: root source inspection and existing completed GitHub code/security reviews found no findings. The author also records an independent source review without Major/Medium findings.
- Existing PR validation is retained as development evidence: #346 plugin selection 223 PASS; #347 related selection 203 PASS / 2 conditional Docker skips and quick suite 667 PASS. The integrated release commit receives a fresh mandatory full suite and same-commit Linux/Windows CI; counts from earlier candidates are not final-release counts.
- Final receipts, source/archive identities, review dispositions, actual Worker/model startup and usage estimates are retained under `_testenv/releases/0.16.14/`.

## Release scope

One integrated main commit and one `.tgz`/SHA-256 are fixed before candidate preflight, the mandatory full suite and native Worker/model startup. The same archive is installed into both global CLI prefixes and OpenCode's config-local dependency, attached to GitHub Release and published once to npm. Existing model overrides and unrelated settings are preserved.

Fixture success and Worker startup do not establish completion of the original external-project tasks or formal benchmark scoring. Shared OpenCode service restart remains user-controlled; installed identity and shared-host loaded identity are reported separately.

## Verified candidate

- Commit: `d4c312beb87c57d22b6dd30f9c2c82a879f1ab50`.
- Archive SHA-256: `05ba17633826f688c95c0d469f1690270a8066f02562c8cfc5a46babd521b0d1`.
- Linux full: 2593 passed, 4 skipped, 136 files. Windows CI: 55/55 passed on the same commit.
- Actual Worker: `openai/gpt-6.1-terra#max`, startup 15949 ms; Operator `openai/gpt-6.1-sol#xhigh`. Startup usage estimate $0.06011960; 2 unpriced requests. Final-archive startup only.
- Existing PR bodies/reviews/ordinary/inline comments collected and classified; no outstanding findings. Shared service not automatically restarted.

releases.name: v0.16.13 — Native Git index and mkdir operand fixes
releases.body:
# v0.16.13 — Native Git index and mkdir operand fixes

## Changes

- Inspect the repository actually selected by native shell Location/workdir before a Git commit, including authorized external clones and subdirectory execution. Inspect the whole index with `--no-relative`; preflight never stages, unstages or commits files.
- Include preceding explicit `git add` paths in the prospective index. Preserve scope and explicit caller prohibitions, including when the Mission project and native Location differ. Command-local directory/index overrides and unsupported Git mutation forms retain their existing refusal behavior.
- Reconcile Git's physical repository paths with symlinked workspace and external-clone spellings. Resolve workspace-root aliases while preserving index-relative pathname components; retain physical and authorized alias paths for caller checks.
- Authorize staged symbolic links as directory entries, including dangling links. Entry authorization does not grant writes through their targets. Existing ordinary file-write checks remain in force.
- Preserve missing directory scope components and compare indexed paths independently of current working-tree directory symlinks. Neither a missing directory nor a replaced ancestor can authorize unrelated staged entries.
- Parse `mkdir -m` / `--mode` values separately from directory operands, including attached values, combined flags and `--`. Fix the observed native command being rejected for a nonexistent `<workdir>/700` write, while retaining checks on every actual directory and redirect.

## Review and verification

PR #343 initially had two valid P2 findings: symlinked workspace paths were incorrectly rejected, and staged links were treated as target writes. Both were reproduced against `50d523fca15078c614da5a216926ec8c5998b32d`. Follow-up review found two valid regressions in the first correction (`87186f1`): missing directory scopes widened to their existing ancestor, and mutable working-tree ancestry could change indexed-path authorization. Both were also reproduced before correction. The final plugin, manifest, shell-workdir and shell-sink selection passed 242 tests in 21.662 seconds, reusing the successful unchanged build after correcting fixture-only index cleanup. A real Git add from a symlinked native cwd verifies prospective physical-cwd semantics. Existing wrong-clone, staged-out-of-scope, caller-prohibition, command-context and real fixture-commit coverage is retained.

The final integrated main commit and one `.tgz`/SHA-256 are fixed before candidate preflight, the mandatory full suite and actual Worker/model startup. The same archive is used for global installation, GitHub Release and one npm publication. Final receipts, review dispositions, failure/success logs and model cost records are retained under `_testenv/releases/0.16.13/`.

The additional `mkdir` failure was recovered from the saved native tool input and reproduced before correction. The plugin, shell-mkdir, shell-workdir, shell-sink and release-profile selection passed 230 tests in 30.409 seconds including build. The regression covers the original compound command, mode syntax variants, real numeric/dash-named operands, redirect scope checks and actual Linux creation with mode `0700`. This runtime correction supersedes the unpublished Git-only archive; the new archive receives fresh release gates.

The fixture's actual Git commit and symlink regressions are model-free checks, not replay of the original user's separate-clone task or formal benchmark scoring. The final-archive native CLI gate verifies startup/model identity. Existing model overrides and unrelated global settings are preserved; running shared-host identity is verified separately after a user-chosen restart.

## Verified candidate

- Commit: `2a97b31e7be92a757abd69bd9dede23a317da010`.
- Archive SHA-256: `d9a8a9c0608f0d8f9b4ae2dc19cc53d0b5dc98020cc44ad356709e4237ec2630`.
- Linux full: 2586 passed, 4 skipped, 136 files. Windows CI: 55/55

releases.name: v0.16.12 — Mission-native Fabric and conditional Scout diagnosis
releases.body:
# v0.16.12 — Mission-native Fabric and conditional Scout diagnosis

## Changes

- Allow two independent Luna implementation units to execute concurrently in separate managed worktrees within the existing Mission lifecycle. Preserve per-unit Goal reservations and settlement, candidate integration, formal validation, independent Review, cancellation and recovery. Dirty bases, overlapping or uncertain dependencies, unavailable preparation and incompatible explicit model choices retain the serial path.
- Execute combined-candidate checks through ordinary native shell calls and host hooks. Preserve native `deny`/`ask` decisions, bind evidence to the exact actor/call/candidate/command/directory and never turn refusal or missing completion evidence into PASS. A host-bound one-time interrupted-check retry retains prior accounting and reevaluates native permissions.
- Preserve other Missions' owned dirty worktrees during reconciliation, allow explicit retry after settled sibling failures, and generate integration patches independently of `diff.noprefix`. Retain the V1 named factory's numeric-exit completion contract without accepting missing exits or explicit errors/cancellation.
- Reuse existing Scouts for conditional parallel failure diagnosis when independent unresolved questions can change the repair. Known causes and cheap local investigation use the normal correction path; diagnosis is optional and does not create retry or rescue prerequisites.
- Preserve the currently selected OAuth route when seeding isolated CLI fixtures. Shared authentication and model defaults remain unchanged.

Integrated source PRs: #338, #339, #340 and #341. The existing six valid Fabric review findings were resolved through targeted corrections and related regression tests; CI success was not treated as finding resolution. See `docs/mission-fabric-late-review-20261107.md`.

## Retained native evidence and limits

- A fixed pre-release package completed two actual `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast#max` Workers, separate worktrees, combined-candidate native checks, independent Review PASS and Mission acceptance. Operator/Coordinator/Reviewer used `openai/gpt-6.1-sol#xhigh`.
- One same-package two-file comparison observed parallel at 269.268 seconds / $0.37528512 and serial at 274.891 seconds / $0.29740900. Cache/provider/load conditions were uncontrolled; the small time difference and higher observed parallel cost do not establish general speed or cost superiority.
- A natural saved-failure request voluntarily selected two parallel Scouts and handed their findings to a Terra/max Worker. It completed in 327.139 seconds / $0.31729072, versus 258.146 seconds / $0.26070580 for a same-package Worker-only companion. Both passed formal validation and Review; Worker read counts were eight in both arms. One Scout file-not-found recovered. These single-fixture observations do not justify automatic routing thresholds or broader parallelism.
- Comparisons use retained development packages, not the final release archive. Reflection's behavioral benefit and Advisor's effect on parent decisions remain unproven. No automatic model router or three-to-five-lane expansion is introduced. No formal public benchmark score is claimed. Token-price estimates exclude parent development chat and browser consultation billing.

## Release verification

The release routine fixes the integrated main commit and one archive/SHA-256, then runs candidate preflight, the mandatory full suite and actual final-archive Worker/model startup before global installation, tagging, GitHub Release and a single npm publication of that same archive. Successful source-level native completion evidence is reused instead of repeating those model tasks. Final receipts are retained under `_testenv/releases/0.16.12/`.

releases.body:
# v0.16.11 — Advisor per-request consultation scope

## Changes

- Clarify that each host-admitted Strategy request covers one candidate and one focused question, not a reused Advisor session's entire lifetime. A previous answer alone does not consume an invented consultation slot or require a fresh Advisor session.
- Evaluate the current admitted question, new evidence and explicit corrections; earlier advice is context, not authority over current constraints. Preserve existing host admission, duplicate/retry controls, explicit budgets, tool-free advice, no implementation and no SourceReview. Advice grants no execution, retry, scope or budget authority and is not validation or acceptance.
- The canonical Advisor body renders into the Mission profile. No consultation helper/config API, host counter, model default, permission, Mission state, dependency or budget change. Only package/runtime identity advances for this release.

## Investigation and bounded evidence

The user's screenshot was traced to a saved native Advisor history: the host delivered a second distinct question with new observations, but the actual `openai/gpt-6-astra#xhigh` Advisor refused because it had previously answered one Strategy request. This was a model-visible refusal, not evidence of a host quota denial. The exact historical assembled provider request was not captured; the wording is not claimed as its sole historical cause.

The requested authenticated ChatGPT browser consultation recommended a local wording fix rather than disposable Advisor sessions, new IDs/counters or public helper/config changes. Only public source snippets and anonymized facts were shared. See `docs/investigations/advisor-request-boundary-20261106.md`.

A controlled native CLI rendering probe used the same actual Astra/xhigh model and two synthetic questions per retained primary-mode session. The old body refused the second question; the new body returned two concrete explanations and one recommendation about the new runtime/checker observations while preserving unmeasured performance. Four replies, no tools or child sessions: **139.622 seconds / $0.180396 / zero unpriced requests**. This is a primary-mode adaptation of the rendered body, not native Coordinator/Advisor child Task integration, original GPU-task recovery, official scoring, universal compliance or a speed/quality comparison. Browser/author billing is unmeasured, not zero.

Before the fix, new contract/profile checks produced 152 passes / 2 expected failures. After the fix, related Fast-lane, packed-loader, V010-runtime and Mission-completion checks passed **204/204**, exit 0, 23.143 seconds. Same-trigger/candidate/reused-child admission is covered alongside unchanged duplicate, unauthorized/exhausted fallback and invalid-trigger denials.

The already-running feature full completed with **2,547 PASS / 4 skip**, 134 files, exit 0, 421.935 seconds. Release-profile identity checks then passed **4/4**, 8.401 seconds. These are retained source/preparation observations, not a substitute for final integrated candidate gates.

releases.name: v0.16.10 — Useful early parallel Scout discovery
releases.body:
# v0.16.10 — Useful early parallel Scout discovery

## Changes

- Restore early, concrete repository discovery instead of waiting for a proven blocking evidence gap. Fast-first Operator, Mission Coordinator and canonical routing share one policy: zero Scouts when existing evidence or direct work is sufficient, one for one useful question, and two or three independent useful questions in one parallel foreground round. No mandatory-three ritual, extra Coordinator or preparation unit.
- Scout uses native Read/Glob/Grep to follow relevant callers and tests. Known paths become seeds/search areas rather than a four-path read allowlist. Remove the 120-line, one-read-per-path and 800-character instruction limits; retain eight steps, Luna Fast max, existing question codes/four JSON keys and native host permissions. Shell/web/edits/child dispatch remain outside Scout.
- Reuse source path/line facts and unresolved risks in the next Worker's objective/handoff context. Required author source inspection and validation freshness remain legitimate. Discovery is not validation, independent Review or acceptance.
- Early root Scouts now use the existing Mission consultation recording/model/outcome/result/reload path even before an implementation run exists. Existing Reviewer generated-task/source checks, Advisor routing, execution grants, Worker budget and formal root acceptance remain unchanged.

## Source evidence and limits

PR #335 includes the user-requested completed ChatGPT browser consultation and adoption/source checks in `docs/investigations/scout-initial-discovery-20261106.md`. Existing PR body/submitted/ordinary/inline reviews are collected before integration and publication; CI is not finding resolution. No original private task, session, DB, ledger, model or budget was modified or replayed.

The fixed source pilot demonstrated three actual Luna Fast max Scouts dispatched in the same foreground tool round, discovery beyond the two seed files and decisive lines beyond 120, useful source facts/uncertainty in the actual Worker handoff, one Terra max Worker fix, passing public check, independent fixture Reviewer PASS and formal acceptance. Native CLI elapsed 303.105 seconds; estimated priced usage $0.30676588, zero unpriced requests. One root-model Task-reference transcription was correctly rejected and repaired in the same unit before Worker launch; it is retained rather than hidden.

The pilot explicitly requested the discovery route and had substantial overlap between Scout reads. It does not prove autonomous default utilization, causal speed/cost savings or matched quality superiority. No official/hidden benchmark score is claimed. Browser/author billing is unmeasured, not zero. The completed source pilot is reused rather than replayed solely for this release.

## Release verification boundary

Fix an integrated main commit and one archive/SHA-256, perform packed preflight, one mandatory full suite, same-commit CI and actual Worker/model startup, then apply/attach/publish the same archive once. Final source verification was 285 targeted passes and 2,545 full passes/4 platform skips; final package/main results are recorded separately, not inferred from those earlier receipts.

Use the proven short physical tmpfs environment and the already-diagnosed active-credential selection only in copied isolated verification tooling; shared authentication and production helper source are unchanged. Preserve explicit models and unrelated global/project configuration across global installation and asset initialization. Do not restart the shared OpenCode service automatically. Installed archive/asset identity is separate from loaded identity in a running host.

Release evidence: `_testenv/releases/0.16.10/`. Source/pilot evidence: `_testenv/investigations/20261106-scout-discovery/`.
